data.gender_notes: Kira is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Kira was a goddess of the harvest, the earth, and the fertile fields. The name Kira has its roots in the Greek word 'kēros' meaning 'maiden,' 'young woman,' or 'beloved.' It was also a popular name in ancient Sparta, the land of the legendary warrior-women. The name Kira carries the meaning “Maiden, young woman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kira usually hope their child will grow to embody maiden, young woman and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Kira
in_latin.long_meaning: Kira, femina fortis et septem, dolor et vox, nomen est fortis et sanctum in Ecclesia. Origine, Kira est nomen Graecum, sed in Latinis Ecclesiis est usitatum. In Ecclesiis Latinis, Kira est nomen feminarum fortes et septem, qui habent dolor et vocem in Ecclesia. Nomen Kira est fortis et sanctum, quia in Ecclesia habet virtutem et fidem.
